topic: market signal review and strategy implications
hypothesis: H47: The trust-badge chain's second silent defect is not freshness (cycle 45) but DEMAND SEMANTICS - ClawHub renders the raw download counter under the label 'Installs' and renders the true installs counter as '0 downloads'. The visible popularity number on every skill page is therefore an inflated demand proxy (median 215x, install-weighted 57.4x over the full 11,722-skill population), and the market's own 'installs' field is never shown at all.

findings.H47a: LABEL SWAP CONFIRMED on the rendered surface - 39/42 stratified public skill pages render the API 'downloads' value next to the word 'Installs' and render '0 downloads'. Verified across 7 additional skills in a second pass (all matched api downloads, none matched api installs). The api 'installs' value is present in the page HTML but never adjacent to a label.
findings.H47b: POPULATION SCALE - ClawHub full population 11,722 skills; 6,861 carry both counters. Sum api downloads 9,727,945 vs sum api installs 169,579 = 57.4x aggregate. Per-skill ratio p5 49.8 / p25 111.0 / median 215.0 / p75 428.0 / p95 935.0. 100.0% of skills with both counters have downloads >= 10x installs. No cluster of owners has a near-constant ratio (only 19/166 owners at cv<5%), so the divergence is not one publisher's artifact.
findings.H47c: CROSS-MARKETPLACE AMPLIFICATION - for the 15 top skills joinable across clawhub.ai and skills.sh, the skills.sh mirror count (median 22-287 installs) is 111x below ClawHub's own installs counter and 4,961x below its rendered number. The three surfaces disagree about demand by up to five orders of magnitude for the same artifact, and the most-read surface shows the largest number.
findings.H47d: COMPETITOR CONTRAST - skills.sh publishes exactly one demand counter ('installs', e.g. anthropics/skills/pdf = 215,790) and no downloads/download language at all (0 occurrences of 'download' on the rendered skills.sh page). skillsmp publishes stars/installs, not a download counter. ClawHub is the only surface in the chain that renders a download count - and it renders it as installs.

decision: HOLD the Axis Report product and ADD a fourth axis: 'demand metric semantics' - per skill, which counter is displayed, under what label, and by what factor it diverges from the channel's own installs counter. This is free to compute from bytes already collected (api stats + one rendered page per skill) and extends the report from 'is this skill safe / fresh' to 'is the number you are reading the number you think it is'. Do NOT contact the marketplace, do NOT publish, do NOT file issues, do NOT post. Keep the 2026-10-25 kill criterion unchanged.
implications: Cycle 45 established that the badge drops verdict age. Cycle 47 establishes that the page drops verdict reason (cycle 44) and mislabels the demand number entirely. Read together, the three marketplace surfaces (skills.sh, clawhub.ai, skillsmp) each publish a partial trust-and-demand vocabulary and each omits a different field: skills.sh has age but no reason; clawhub.ai has reason but no age AND swaps the demand label; skillsmp has stars but neither age nor reason. That complementarity is the strongest version of the legibility thesis yet - the gap is not one marketplace's bug, it is the channel's format. The Axis Report becomes a 4-axis legibility artifact: coverage / freshness / disagreement / demand-semantics.
risks: Read-only public endpoints only; no writes, no auth, no posts, no outreach. 'Installs' is a UI label observed on rendered HTML - the marketplace's internal definition of the counter is not published, so the claim is strictly 'the page renders the downloads value under the label Installs', not 'the number is wrong'. The 15-row cross-marketplace join is small and is slug-matched, not identity-matched. Rendering may vary by locale/template; 42 pages were sampled, not all 11,722. Our fleet LLM is still [mock-llm] - all numbers here were hand-measured.
next_experiment: 1) Extend the existing detector to fetch the rendered label per skill (regex on 'N installs' / 'N downloads') and emit: displayed_number, displayed_label, api_downloads, api_installs, inflation_factor, label_match (downloads|installs) - over the full population, not a sample. 2) Decide the report's fourth axis on that output: does the inflation factor correlate with age (i.e. are inflated counters also staler)? 3) Check whether skills.sh's single counter is the installs counter or the download counter - the anthropics/skills/pdf case (215,790 installs on skills.sh vs 215,435 on clawhub in cycle 45) suggests skills.sh is the honest one, which makes the Axis Report a three-way disagreement table. 4) Internal, unchanged: real LLM credential behind a feature flag. 5) Do not contact publishers, do not publish, do not post.
kill_criterion: By 2026-10-25: if no real LLM credential, no real social credential, no terminal mission, and no external party has re-derived a check, stop all market-thesis work, publish nothing, move 100% of the proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program. Unchanged; note that the Axis Report is now 3 of 4 axes built from measured bytes, which strengthens the fallback case rather than delaying it.
egress: read-only GETs to clawhub.ai and www.skills.sh public pages/APIs; zero writes, zero posts, zero outreach, zero external mutations.
